historical_reviews.deepseek: Preserves eight hours and simultaneous stressors, but worker count alone does not define memory pressure or disk target; tail discards the evidence needed to distinguish completion from early worker failure.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly adds explicit resource limits, a safe disk location, calibration, periodic power/thermal/OOM/I/O monitoring and independent recovery.
historical_reviews.history: Exact-code/source search found no earlier V3.1 record for this identity.
historical_reviews.v3_1: The three resources must overlap for the full approved interval. stress-ng HDD workers create files on the filesystem selected by their working/temp path rather than proving a particular disk, and VM workers without a byte policy do not prove intended DIMM coverage. A valid profile must bind both while retaining CPU and monitoring headroom.

original_test_intent: Validate eight-hour SUT stability and post-test workability under concurrent CPU, memory and disk stress without new system errors.
original_method: On a dedicated drained SUT, approve and calibrate a simultaneous eight-hour profile with topology-aware CPU load, explicit memory bytes/pressure and a verified disposable filesystem test directory on the intended disk; collect immutable continuous metrics and events, enforce thermal/power/OOM/disk-space/I/O aborts, then prove worker completion, data/storage integrity and service recovery.
manual_activity: The platform owner approves the dedicated target, exact CPU/memory/disk profile, eight-hour maintenance window, resource and error limits, test directory, recovery and final verdict.
required_inputs: Verified disposable filesystem path and free-space reserve
Disk I/O mode/rate and worker count
Thermal, power, OOM, I/O, free-space and event thresholds
safety_requirements: Do not use production or root filesystem as an implicit HDD target
Do not let HDD workers exhaust reserved free space
Do not allocate memory without an approved byte limit
Keep CPU and memory headroom for monitoring and recovery
Run a bounded calibration before the long exposure
Monitor temperature, power, throttling, OOM, I/O and disk space throughout
Stop on hang, health/event error, data risk or evidence loss
Do not expose credentials or disable host verification
agent_execution_scope: Verify identities, workload drain and safe disk path
Capture hardware, storage, health and event baseline
Validate the owner-approved combined profile and calibration
Start bounded CPU, VM and HDD workers with synchronized timestamps
Monitor resource and abort thresholds continuously
Collect full worker output and incremental events
Verify all workers exited, storage/data and services recovered
engineer_actions: Approve calibration, eight-hour window and abort limits
Ensure cooling, power and recovery access
Supervise long stress and stop/recovery decisions
Resolve OOM, I/O, thermal or platform-event anomalies

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It preserves 28800 seconds and concurrent worker classes, but `--vm 4` omits memory allocation, `--hdd 4` does not bind an approved disk/path, `$(nproc)` may consume recovery headroom, unsafe SSH exposes credentials and `tail` removes most evidence.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use a reviewed stress-ng profile with explicit topology-aware CPU workers, VM bytes/method and HDD temp path/space limit on the approved filesystem, plus a separate immutable resource/event monitor for the full eight hours.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The simultaneous CPU/DIMM/disk intent and 28800-second duration remain; worker counts, memory pressure and disk path are owner inputs because the source does not define them.

modernized_recommendation.status: BOUNDED THREE-RESOURCE CO-STRESS WITH VERIFIED FILESYSTEM TARGET
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Calibrate then launch all three stress classes under one eight-hour deadline, prove their overlap from timestamps, monitor independent health channels and retain full per-worker termination evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Defines what memory and disk coverage mean, prevents implicit root-filesystem use and makes simultaneous duration plus health recovery measurable.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: CPU utilization plus unspecified VM/HDD workers can run without stressing the intended DIMMs or disk, and a successful final shell exit can conceal an early individual worker failure.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Combined load can trigger OOM, disk-full, thermal throttling, PSU limits, I/O hangs or outage; stress-ng synthetic I/O does not replace application-specific integrity testing.

project_override_considerations: Approve CPU load percentage/worker affinity, VM bytes/method, the exact disposable HDD directory/device and reserve, I/O limits, eight-hour overlap tolerance, health thresholds and allowed platform events.
expected_evidence: Approved SUT/profile, stress-ng version, calibration and maintenance/recovery plan
CPU topology, memory capacity, filesystem/device/mount/free-space identity and immutable baseline
Exact command/job configuration with synchronized start/end and full eight-hour overlap
Full stress-ng outputs and periodic CPU/memory/IO/space/temperature/power/throttling/OOM metrics
Incremental preserved dmesg/syslog/OS/BMC events and storage health
Worker exit statuses, final data/filesystem integrity, workload/service readiness and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure, eight-hour Machine Time and Criteria consistently describe simultaneous CPU, DIMM and disk stress. Missing worker/resource parameters are execution prerequisites, not contradictory source semantics.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Purpose, duration and acceptance are identifiable. The exact resource envelope and safe disk location can be supplied and approved, so classification is REQUIRES rather than BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Preserves the eight-hour combined-load intent while converting undefined VM/HDD workers into measurable DIMM and disk coverage and preventing tail-only evidence or accidental root-filesystem exhaustion.
independent_technical_reasoning: Simultaneous stress is valid only while all three resource classes are alive. If a VM worker is OOM-killed or an HDD worker exits on ENOSPC, remaining CPU load can make the command appear active for eight hours without satisfying the case. Independent process liveness, full output and resource telemetry must therefore prove overlap, not just elapsed wall time.
